brief: A lap analysis tool for Formula 1 telemetry: two drivers' laps on synced speed, throttle and brake traces, a delta-time line, a track map coloured by who is faster, lap ratings against the field and a physics-simulated perfect lap. Native macOS app, Windows app and static web app. The mark should tell a story, be simple yet emotionally complicated, and feel as if F1 and Apple had a child.
criteria: Success: one idea per mark, a story in two sentences, tension inside the simplicity, reads at 16 px and in one colour, sits naturally in a macOS dock. No cars, helmets, wheels or fruit; not two racing lines through a corner (the current icon).

concepts.name: Ghost
concepts.idea: You (the solid disc) and the ghost of your better lap (the ring) a hundredth ahead. They never touch.
rationale: Two primitives, one gap: Apple-level restraint, reads at 16 px
The ghost car is how F1 visualises the chase; here it is your own better self
Tension: presence vs. absence, almost touching, forever

concepts.name: Delta
concepts.idea: The delta glyph; its hollow leans forward - the time you have not found yet.
rationale: The one symbol every timing screen shares
Heavy trailing side, hairline leading side: motion without speed lines
Risk: rounded triangles can read as a warning sign

concepts.name: Pulse
concepts.idea: A speed trace through one corner bends around the apex and never touches it.
rationale: Drawn from the app's own speed trace: flat out, brake, the long climb back
Doubles as a heartbeat and a held breath
Risk: thin at 16 px; leans toward a tick

concepts.name: Slipped Square
concepts.idea: The chequered flag with one square slipped out of line: the hundredth you left on track.
rationale: Racing heritage used once, as nine squares
Second reading: a die showing five - precision vs. luck

concepts.name: Hundredth
concepts.idea: The number the whole app exists to explain, with its last digit in red.
rationale: Timing-screen numerals drawn soft and round
The smallest number carrying the greatest weight
Needs a small-size cut (.01) below 32 px

recommendation: Ghost - the simplest form with the deepest story. Two shapes, one gap; it reads at 16 px, survives one colour, feels at home in a macOS dock, and it is the app's whole purpose (chasing a better version of a lap) in one glance.
next_steps: Pick a direction (or tell me what you like in each)
Refine geometry, colour and small-size cut
Replace the app icon (Mac .icns, Windows .ico, web favicon)
